correctness.rationale: The source update was specialized directly to the three scalar blocks and two identity-dynamics constraints. Exact elimination factors the five-state characteristic polynomial into an always-Schur quadratic and a cubic. A recursive Schur transform of the cubic gives necessary-and-sufficient inequalities. The remaining Schur inequalities were proved redundant under the two final conditions. The block-Hessian condition and the source bounded-level assumption were checked independently. Exact rational replay from the packaged artifact reproduces the characteristic factorization and the chi=4 boundary.

originality.rationale: The primary source gives a general Lyapunov sufficient parameter procedure, not an exact equal-parameter spectral frontier. The closest quadratic and three-block ADMM literature either assumes positive-semidefinite/positive-definite block curvature, uses direct nonproximal ADMM, randomization, or a different extended proximal update. Targeted database and web searches found no statement implying the two exact inequalities or the strong-convexity-versus-global-stability gap.
residual_risks: Complete theorem-level text of the 2018 three-block quadratic ADMM paper was not obtainable through the available lawful routes; its accessible stated hypotheses are convex positive-semidefinite and its displayed iteration is nonproximal.
The multiblock ADMM literature is extensive, so an equivalent special-case matrix calculation under different notation could exist outside the searched sources.
The finding is for equal penalties and equal proximal parameters and does not claim sharpness for the source's full unequal-parameter family.

value.rationale: The three-state identity chain is the smallest genuinely multiblock instance of the source dynamics model, while the sign pattern of the block quadratics gives a constrained strongly convex objective with one locally concave block. The exact frontier separates two notions often conflated in parameter tuning: making every primal subproblem strongly convex and stabilizing the full coupled primal-dual Gauss--Seidel map. The open gap at chi=4 and the no-stable-common-parameter threshold chi=9 are structurally meaningful design facts for a newly proposed proximal multiblock method rather than arbitrary numerical slices.
